messages:
Maya Patel: Hey team — over the last 30m our integration started getting 429s and user-facing errors. We're on the Team paid plan (acct id: team-42). We were doing bursts of 150 requests/s for short windows (~20s) and most calls fail with 429s. Error response includes \"quota_exhausted\" and sometimes \"rate_limit\". Can you explain why we're seeing this despite being on paid plan? Need advice on short-term workaround and how to get a permanent increase.

Samir Khan: Sorry about the disruption, Maya. Can you paste one of the raw responses (headers + body) and the request id if present? Also confirm which endpoint: /v1/generate or /v1/embeddings?

Maya Patel: Pasting one of the responses (redacted token):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r-1a2b3c4d
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1719601283
Retry-After: 12
{
  "error": {
    "type": "quota_exhausted",
    "message": "Request rate limit exceeded for project team-42"
  }
}
```
We're hitting this on /v1/embeddings mostly. SDK is node; we do ~150 parallel embedding calls per second in short bursts.

Olivia Chen: Thanks, this is helpful. The headers show a per-account token rate limit of 100 r/s for the embeddings endpoint on your current paid tier. The X-RateLimit-* values confirm a hard ceiling, and Retry-After indicates how long the gateway expects you to wait. Bursts above the steady rate will be throttled unless you have a larger burst allowance or Dedicated capacity.

Olivia Chen: Quick guidance: 1) Implement exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. 2) Use batch embeddings (we have a batch endpoint that accepts up to 256 items and is more efficient). 3) Add a token-based queue in your client to smooth bursts (leaky bucket / token bucket). 4) For immediate relief, we can request a temporary overage window while sales processes a quota bump.

Samir Khan: Repro steps I asked the customer to run to help root cause: 1) Run a single-threaded script that sends 150 requests/s for 30s to /v1/embeddings with your API key and capture headers. 2) Run again but with the SDK's built-in batching disabled (to confirm it's per-request load). 3) Collect gateway response headers for three failing requests.

Maya Patel: I ran the script. Same behavior and same headers. We rely on user-initiated workflows that can spike. Batching isn't trivial for our current UX. Can you escalate to sales for a plan increase or get a temporary exception?

Samir Khan: Looping in Rafael from Sales for quota increases — @Rafael Torres can you advise on process for a short-term increase and whether we can do a temporary exception while the billing contract updates?

Rafael Torres: Hey all — we can escalate. Two quick asks: (1) what's the target r/s you need sustained and peak burst target; (2) who is the billing contact and PO if applicable. For short-term exceptions we can approve a 24–72 hour window in many cases, but anything longer requires a commit/upgrade. Maya, what are the numbers?

Maya Patel: Ideally sustained 200 r/s with bursts up to 400 r/s for ~10–30s. Billing contact is ops+billing@acme.inc. We prefer not to upgrade permanently if we can optimize client-side.

Rafael Torres: OK. I'll open a ticket with finance/legal for a short-term overage and prepare a quote for Dedicated/Reserved capacity which is the standard solution for predictable high-throughput needs. Dedicated gives you a guaranteed pool and avoids shared token limits. I'll need the customer account id and a request for SLA window.

Samir Khan: Internal note for SRE/infra: looks like current token-level limits are enforced gateway-side using a 1s sliding window + burst smoothing. Could infra check whether we have an undone configuration that caps team-42 lower than expected?

Olivia Chen: Checked logs — team-42 is on the Paid Team plan with default embeddings quota 100 r/s and a small burst buffer of +25%. The bursts you described (400 r/s) exceed that. No misconfiguration seen.

billing-bot: Alert: Account team-42 exceeded soft quota threshold at 1719601200. Auto-notice sent to billing + customer.

Samir Khan: Next steps for customer: (a) We can open a temporary overage for 48 hours while sales finalizes the upgrade; (b) Implement Retry-After-based backoff immediately to reduce UX errors; (c) Consider using batch endpoint to reduce request count; (d) If this is a recurring pattern, Dedicated or Reserved capacity is the recommended path.

Maya Patel: Appreciate it. Can I get the exact wording/help we can show our QA team for retry/backoff? Also, is there any way to detect at runtime we're at the bursting edge before requests fail?

Olivia Chen: Sample retry pseudo-code for client (please adapt):
```
let attempts = 0
async function callWithBackoff(req) {
  while (attempts < 5) {
    const res = await fetch('/v1/embeddings', req)
    if (res.status === 200) return res.json()
    if (res.status === 429) {
      const retry = parseInt(res.headers.get('Retry-After') || '1', 10)
      await sleep(retry * 1000 * Math.pow(2, attempts))
      attempts++
      continue
    }
    throw new Error('non-retryable: ' + res.status)
  }
  throw new Error('max retries exceeded')
}
```
Detecting burst edge: watch X-RateLimit-Remaining and latency spikes. If Remaining drops quickly across requests, start queuing/smoothing client side.

Samir Khan: Samir -> Maya: I've submitted a support escalation for a 48h temporary overage (ticket REF: SUP-2024-847). Rafael is working the quote. I'll update this thread once finance confirms.

Rafael Torres: Finance asked for expected monthly token/embedding volume and whether you want a short-term uplift vs permanent upgrade. I'll follow up via email with a draft amendment.

Maya Patel: Thanks, all. One small ask — will we be charged for the temporary overage if usage goes over current committed amount?

Rafael Torres: Temporary overages typically get billed at an overage rate (we can invoice or apply a one-time credit depending on the account). I'll include options in the follow-up email.

Samir Khan: Closing note: engineering tips for prod apps — prefer batching, client-side smoothing, exponential backoff + jitter, instrument X-RateLimit-* headers and expose to ops dashboards, and consider Dedicated for traffic patterns with regular short bursts.

Maya Patel: Great. We'll start with backoff + batching and await the 48h window. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
